take_homes: Start with one agent. Split only for different access, dialect or stance, and ask whether one prompt could do the same job.
The handoffs between agents are where it breaks, and the checks cover those seams. They do not tell you whether the result is true.
Three parallel agents pulled material from our own wiki and docs, and I could do that myself and judge the output.

monday.blocker: Steering groups, and doubt about whether the output can be trusted.

misconception.why: This did not sound like the last programmes. It told me not to use more agents than needed, said what the audit cannot check, and let me test it on our own material. I still think the hype around it may blow over. I am less sure that waiting is the safe move.

one_line: First training in years that told me when not to use the thing, and it admits it can't check whether the answer is right. Still homework-heavy, and I haven't seen it beat a competent analyst yet.
